# Pass 1: grounded GH candidate authoring

This is original unofficial learning material, never an official practice exam.
Read `docs/gh-three-pass-workflow.md`, `docs/source-policy.md`, the current
package objectives, request and source-approval request. Work in the canonical
package: GH-300 = `github-copilot`; GH-600 = `github-agentic-ai-developer`.

Before authoring, actually retrieve the current official Learn study guide,
credential and linked self-paced paths/modules with Microsoft Learn MCP.
Approve only the guide, its/credential-linked Learn training and official Learn
or GitHub Docs pages directly linked or clearly referenced by those roots.
Inspect the exact claim, scope, plan, role, prerequisite, syntax and GA/Preview
status. Never use assessments, blogs, videos, knowledge checks or search
summaries as evidence or inspiration. Stop dependent candidates on retrieval
failure. Preserve actual retrieval timestamps, link/redirect receipts or short
explicit reference passages in `source-registry.json`.

Author in small objective-balanced batches. Target 150 verified **per exam**;
candidate count is a separate planning goal. Planning difficulty mix is
Foundational (`beginner`) 15%, Intermediate 35%, Advanced 35%, Expert 15%.
At least 40% applied reasoning when objectives support it. Unknown weighting
remains unknown. Do not invent skills, pad counts or use cosmetic fact variants.

Write original complete questions, keyed answers, explanations, every
distractor's wrong-in-context distinction, and claim-level source mappings.
Use stable fact-level concept IDs. Include all conditions needed to choose.
Set `verificationStatus: "candidate"` and `requiresManualReview: true`.
Write the generation record in `validation-metadata.json`, with your actual
author ID/date, exact question/objective fingerprints and every option's
grounded claim. Do not create technical/adversarial reviews or scores.

Run metadata-only custom-file validation; it does not authorize gameplay.
Hand the unchanged candidates and actual evidence to a different technical
reviewer context. Scaffolding is not generation, a model or evidence.
